## {{< var wip >}} Configuration File

In addition to passing configuration options via command line flags or
python parameters, `flower` can be configured via `pyproject.toml`. The
advantage of doing so is that the formatting can be easier for complex
multi-page documentation sites and that options that are frequently used
can be set once instead of included each time flower is called from the
command line or Python.

### Examples

```{.toml filename="pyproject.toml"}
[tool.flower]
style="quarto-resource-listings"
ci="quarto"
```

Running `build` with this configuration file builds a documentation site
in qmd format for the data package in the current working directory. The
chosen style splits the documentation into several pages. Template files
are included for setting up continuous integration with quarto on
GitHub.

---

```{.toml filename="pyproject.toml"}
[tool.flower]
style="custom"

[[tool.flower.section]]
template="1st-page.html"
content="package"

[[tool.flower.section]]
template="2nd-page.html"
content=[
    "contributors",
    "licenses",
]
```

Running `build` with this configuration file builds a documentation site
in html format for the data package in the current working directory.
The custom style of the documentation creates one page with the package
metadata and a second page with info on the contributors and license.
Both pages are created using a custom HTML template.
